The **Brahmaputra** river, one of Asia's largest, overflowed after days of relentless monsoon rain.
Several rivers remain **above the official danger mark**, keeping the risk of fresh flooding alive.
Large numbers of **livestock have died**, threatening rural livelihoods and raising disease risks.
stories.background: Assam, in India's northeast, sits along the Brahmaputra river system and floods almost every monsoon season (roughly June to September), though severity varies year to year with rainfall. This year's monsoon has brought unusually intense, sustained rain, pushing the Brahmaputra and its tributaries well past danger levels across the state. The state's disaster response is coordinated by the Assam State Disaster Management Authority (ASDMA), which tracks river levels and runs relief camps. Floods like this one are a near-annual test of India's disaster preparedness in one of its most flood-prone regions.
stories.what_happened: The death toll from Assam's ongoing floods reached **100** on Monday, August 10, after two more people died overnight. Days of relentless monsoon rain caused the **Brahmaputra** — which flows roughly 900 km through Assam — and other rivers to overflow, inundating villages, sweeping away homes, and forcing nearly **300,000 people** into government-run relief camps at the crisis's peak. About **49,000 people remain** in **125 relief camps and distribution centers**, even as floodwaters recede in some areas and residents begin returning home. Several rivers remain above the official danger mark, according to ASDMA, meaning the risk of fresh flooding hasn't passed. The floods have also killed large numbers of livestock, hurting rural livelihoods and raising fears of disease outbreaks in the affected areas.
stories.why_it_matters: A death toll of 100 and displacement of hundreds of thousands makes this one of the more severe flood disasters India has faced this monsoon season, straining state resources and testing disaster-response infrastructure in a region that floods almost every year. It's also a reminder that shifts in monsoon intensity are making these 'routine' annual floods progressively more destructive.
stories.ripple_effects: Displaced families face the immediate risk of waterborne disease outbreaks in crowded relief camps, while destroyed crops and dead livestock threaten rural incomes for months to come. Damaged roads, bridges, and embankments will require costly state and central government reconstruction spending. Continued high river levels mean the disaster isn't over — any new heavy rainfall could reverse the recovery already underway.
stories.why_now: The toll crossed 100 on August 10 as two more deaths were confirmed overnight, marking a grim milestone in a flood crisis that has been building for days as monsoon rains intensified.
stories.watch_next: Watch river levels against the official danger mark over the coming days — if they rise again, the roughly 49,000 people still in relief camps could grow rather than shrink.

key_terms.definition: One of Asia's largest rivers, flowing from Tibet through northeast India and into Bangladesh — its seasonal flooding shapes life across Assam every monsoon.

stories.the_lesson: Annual, 'expected' disasters like monsoon flooding can still turn into major humanitarian crises once rainfall intensity crosses a threshold — preparedness reduces damage, but it doesn't eliminate it when the rain is severe enough.

stories.title: Parliament passes bill letting government allow charges on UPI payments — Sitharaman says users pay nothing, Opposition unconvinced
key_points: The **Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026** cleared the Rajya Sabha on **August 10**, after the Lok Sabha passed it the week before.
It amends the payments law to let the government **permit banks and payment firms to charge fees on UPI** for the first time.
Finance Minister **Nirmala Sitharaman** called it only an 'enabling provision' and promised **no charges for consumers or small merchants**.
Opposition MP **Sanjay Singh** called her assurance 'contradictory and misleading' and alleged the bill came under **pressure from the US**.
The bill also adds tax breaks for **data-centre services** and incentives for the **diamond trade**.
stories.background: UPI (Unified Payments Interface) is India's instant, phone-based payment system, run by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), and has become the backbone of everyday digital payments across the country — from street vendors to online shopping — largely because it has always been **free** for users and merchants. That free-ness has also made UPI a competitive threat to card networks like Visa and Mastercard, whose merchant fees UPI undercuts entirely. Until now, the law governing digital payments had no clause explicitly allowing anyone to charge fees on UPI transactions. This new bill inserts that clause for the first time, even though the government insists it has no immediate plan to use it.
stories.what_happened: Parliament passed the **Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026** — the Lok Sabha approved it the previous week, and the **Rajya Sabha cleared it on Monday evening, August 10**, after a brief but heated debate that saw the Opposition walk out. As a Money Bill, the Rajya Sabha could only suggest changes before sending it back to the Lok Sabha. Its most contested provision amends Section 10A of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act to let the central government permit banks and payment providers to levy charges on **UPI and other digital payment modes — a legal power that didn't exist before**. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman told the House this is merely an 'enabling provision,' not an actual fee, and that any future decision on a Merchant Discount Rate (the fee a merchant pays a bank per transaction) would go through NPCI's UPI oversight committee, with consumers and small merchants continuing to pay nothing. Opposition MP Sanjay Singh directly rebutted her, calling the assurance 'contradictory and misleading' — noting she'd earlier floated a committee to decide 'how much tax' to charge traders — and alleged the bill was introduced under **pressure from the US**, whose government has reportedly wanted UPI monetized after Indians shifted away from Visa and Mastercard toward the free system. The bill separately includes unrelated tax breaks for data-centre services and incentives for the diamond-trading industry.
stories.why_it_matters: UPI processes billions of free transactions a month for ordinary Indians, so any legal opening — however described as merely 'enabling' — to eventually charge fees touches nearly everyone who uses a phone to pay for anything. It also reopens a years-long fight over who should bear the cost of running a payments network that succeeded partly because it was free.
stories.ripple_effects: If fees are ever actually introduced, small merchants and low-income users who rely on free UPI could see new costs, potentially pushing some back toward cash. Banks and payment companies, who have long argued UPI's zero-fee model is financially unsustainable for them, would benefit from a new revenue stream. The political fight also feeds into broader India-US trade tensions, if the Opposition's claim about US pressure gains traction.
stories.why_now: The bill moved through Parliament in its final pre-recess week, alongside other pending legislation like the FCRA bill, and its passage on August 10 immediately triggered the same kind of Opposition pushback seen on the government's other end-of-session bills.
stories.watch_next: Watch NPCI's UPI and Service Operations Committee for any future move to actually set a Merchant Discount Rate — that would be the real test of Sitharaman's 'no charges' promise.

key_terms.definition: Unified Payments Interface — India's free, instant, phone-based payment system run by NPCI, used for everything from paying street vendors to online shopping.
A small fee a merchant pays their bank for processing a digital payment — currently zero for UPI transactions in India.
A category of legislation dealing with taxes or government spending that only needs Lok Sabha approval to become law — the Rajya Sabha can only suggest changes, not block it.

stories.the_lesson: A law can create the legal power to do something — like charge a fee — long before anyone actually uses that power, and the political fight often happens the moment the door opens, not the moment someone walks through it.
stories.market_link: Watch UPI-linked fintech and payments stocks for any repricing on MDR speculation, and traditional card-network names for relief if UPI's cost advantage narrows.

stories.title: Manchester Super Giants crush SunRisers Leeds to move to the brink of a Hundred men's Eliminator spot
key_points: MSG chased down the target in just **67 legal balls**, a dominant run-chase.
The win moved Super Giants above SunRisers Leeds into **second place** in the table.
**Trent Rockets** have already secured their spot straight in the **final**.
**Tim Seifert (80\* not out)** and **Paul Walter (44\* not out)** anchored the chase.
The men's **Eliminator** is set for **Friday, August 14** at the Kia Oval; the final follows at Lord's on **August 16**.
stories.background: The Hundred is English cricket's short-format franchise competition, with eight men's and eight women's teams playing a round-robin followed by knockouts: the top team goes straight to the final, while the 2nd and 3rd-placed teams meet in an Eliminator for the second final spot. Trent Rockets had already all-but wrapped up top spot heading into the final league games.
stories.what_happened: In the 30th match of the 2026 Hundred men's competition at **Old Trafford, Manchester**, on **August 11**, Manchester Super Giants routed SunRisers Leeds, chasing down their target in just **67 legal balls** thanks to unbeaten innings from **Tim Seifert (80\*)** and **Paul Walter (44\*)**. The result vaulted Super Giants above SunRisers Leeds into second place in the table, putting them on the brink of confirming their place in Friday's Eliminator. **Trent Rockets**, meanwhile, had already secured their place directly in the final by finishing top of the table.
stories.why_it_matters: The result reshuffles the run-in to the knockout stage of one of English cricket's most-watched short-format tournaments, deciding which team gets a straight run to the final (Trent Rockets) and which must fight through the Eliminator for a shot at the title.
stories.ripple_effects: SunRisers Leeds, the defending champions, now face a fight just to stay in playoff contention, while Manchester Super Giants carry momentum into Friday's Eliminator. A strong showing also raises the profile of players like Seifert and Walter ahead of future franchise-league auctions.
stories.why_now: The result came in the final rounds of the group stage, directly shaping which two teams meet in the Eliminator before the August 16 final at Lord's.
stories.watch_next: The men's Eliminator at the Kia Oval on August 14, which decides who joins Trent Rockets in the final.

key_terms.definition: A knockout match in tournaments like The Hundred between the 2nd and 3rd-placed teams from the group stage, with the winner advancing to the final.

stories.the_lesson: In round-robin-plus-playoff formats, finishing position in the last few games can matter more than overall season form — a single dominant late win can flip a team's entire playoff path.

stories.title: Barbados Tridents edge Jamaica Kingsmen by 5 runs in tight CPL opener at Sabina Park
key_points: Barbados Tridents posted **206/3** and held on to beat hosts Jamaica Kingsmen by **5 runs** in Kingston.
Jamaica Kingsmen fell just short, finishing on **201/9** from their 20 overs.
Fast bowler **Daniel Sams** was named Player of the Match for figures of **4/20**.
It's the Tridents' first outing under their restored name, after the Barbados franchise reverted from "Royals" back to **Barbados Tridents** for the 2026 CPL season.
stories.background: The **Caribbean Premier League (CPL)** is the Caribbean's top T20 franchise tournament, running since 2013 and featuring six regional teams stocked with international stars during the Northern Hemisphere's cricket off-season. Barbados's team has changed names before — it was the Tridents in the league's early years before being rebranded the Royals — and the CPL confirmed the **Tridents** name was restored for 2026. Jamaica's franchise, meanwhile, enters this season under a new **Kingsmen** identity, and both teams are opening their campaigns in a tournament where net run rate often decides who reaches the playoffs.
stories.what_happened: Barbados Tridents beat hosts Jamaica Kingsmen by **5 runs** in the 4th match of the 2026 Caribbean Premier League at **Sabina Park, Kingston**, on **August 11**. Batting first, the Tridents posted **206/3** from their 20 overs, built around a strong middle-overs platform. Chasing 207 to win, Jamaica Kingsmen fought hard but finished on **201/9**, falling **5 runs** short despite a late push. Fast bowler **Daniel Sams** was the difference-maker with the ball, taking **4 wickets for 20 runs** to restrict Jamaica's chase, and was named Player of the Match.
stories.why_it_matters: It's an early-season form signal for two franchises that reshaped themselves ahead of 2026 — Barbados reverting to a familiar identity, Jamaica rebranding entirely — and early CPL results start shaping the net-run-rate calculations that often decide playoff qualification in this short-format tournament.
stories.ripple_effects: A strong start gives Barbados Tridents momentum heading into a congested group stage, while Jamaica Kingsmen will need to quickly fix their batting depth to avoid an early points gap that's hard to claw back over a short tournament.
stories.why_now: The match was played on **August 11** as part of the CPL's opening round of fixtures for the 2026 season.
stories.watch_next: Watch Jamaica Kingsmen's next fixture for signs of how they respond to the loss, and whether Daniel Sams' form continues as a bowling weapon for Barbados through the group stage.

key_terms.definition: The Caribbean Premier League — the Caribbean's top T20 franchise cricket tournament, played each August-September.

stories.the_lesson: In short-format cricket, a handful of overs from one bowler having a great day can swing an entire match, which is exactly why T20 franchises pay a premium for proven death-overs specialists.

stories.title: Amnesty International warns Afghanistan's cricket series in Ireland risks becoming 'Taliban propaganda'
key_points: Cricket Ireland has security plans in place with police as it hosts Afghanistan for a **five-match ODI series**, with fixtures at Bready and Belfast's Stormont.
Amnesty International's **Felix Jakens** said the Taliban 'will look to harness this series for propaganda purposes', comparing it to other regimes using sport to launder their image.
The controversy centers on the Taliban's near-total ban on **women's sport, education and public life** since taking power in 2021.
Amnesty is calling on Cricket Ireland and the **ICC** to keep Afghan women's exclusion in focus while still honouring the right to peaceful protest.
stories.background: Afghanistan's men's cricket team continues to compete internationally even though the Taliban government has banned women and girls from playing sport, attending school past a certain age, and taking part in most public life since retaking power in 2021. This tension has repeatedly put other cricket boards — including Australia and England — under pressure over whether continuing to play Afghanistan implicitly legitimizes the Taliban, or whether keeping the team engaged is the better way to keep pressure on the regime.
stories.what_happened: With Ireland hosting Afghanistan for a five-match men's ODI series (two games at Bready, three at Belfast's Stormont, with Stormont fixtures on August 10, 12 and 15), Cricket Ireland has arranged security plans with the Police Service of Northern Ireland in anticipation of demonstrations. Amnesty International spokesperson Felix Jakens told BBC Sport that 'the Taliban will look to harness this series for propaganda purposes,' comparing the dynamic to other regimes using sport to 'launder their image.' Jakens called on Cricket Ireland and the ICC to keep the plight of Afghan women in focus throughout the series and to fully respect the right to peaceful protest around the matches.
stories.why_it_matters: It's a live flashpoint in the broader 'sportswashing' debate — whether engaging a country's national team competitively props up an oppressive government's image, even when the players themselves aren't the ones setting policy.
stories.ripple_effects: Continued controversy could influence how other cricket boards schedule future fixtures against Afghanistan, and adds pressure on the ICC to take a clearer stance on the issue.
stories.why_now: The warning is timed to the ongoing Stormont leg of the series, which continues through August 15.
stories.watch_next: Watch for whether protests materialize at the August 15 Stormont fixture, and any formal response from the ICC.

key_terms.definition: Using participation in or hosting of sports events to improve a government's or regime's international image, distracting from its human-rights record.

stories.the_lesson: Sport and politics are rarely fully separable — international engagement with a country's team can become a proxy battleground over the legitimacy of its government.

stories.title: Former Australia star Moises Henriques to captain Portugal in T20 World Cup qualifiers
key_points: **Moises Henriques**, 39, who retired from Australian domestic cricket last month, will captain **Portugal's** 14-player squad.
The ICC T20 World Cup **Europe Sub-Regional Qualifier C** runs in Finland from **August 14-20**.
Portugal are grouped with **Israel, Germany, Greece and the Czech Republic**; the group winner advances toward a European regional final.
It's part of Portugal's bid to reach a **T20 World Cup for the first time ever**.
stories.background: Cricket's global qualifying system lets 'associate' nations — countries without full Test-playing status — work their way toward major ICC tournaments through regional qualifiers. Henriques, born in Madeira, Portugal, played for Australia internationally and had a long IPL career including with Sunrisers Hyderabad; his Portuguese heritage makes him eligible to represent Portugal, joining a broader trend of established professionals turning out for smaller cricketing nations.
stories.what_happened: Henriques was named captain of Portugal's 14-player squad for the ICC T20 World Cup Europe Sub-Regional Qualifier C, being held in Finland from August 14 to 20, 2026. Portugal are grouped alongside Israel, Germany, Greece and the Czech Republic; the group winner advances toward a European regional final alongside Scotland, Jersey and Denmark, with the top finishers from that stage progressing toward the global qualifying pathway for the 2028 T20 World Cup in Australia and New Zealand. It marks Portugal's push to reach a T20 World Cup for the first time in the country's history. The squad also includes players such as Craig Cachopa, Edward Fleming and wicketkeeper Dhavalkumar Norotam.
stories.why_it_matters: It's a genuine growth-of-the-game story: a recognizable former international lending his experience and profile to help an associate nation chase a first-ever World Cup appearance.
stories.ripple_effects: A strong showing could raise Portugal's cricketing profile domestically and help attract more heritage-eligible players to represent smaller nations, a pattern already seen elsewhere in associate cricket.
stories.why_now: The squad announcement comes just days before the qualifying tournament begins on August 14.
stories.watch_next: Watch Portugal's results in the Finland qualifier group stage, starting August 14.

key_terms.definition: A cricket-playing country that is an ICC member but hasn't attained full Test-playing 'Full Member' status; most World Cup qualifying pathways run through these nations.

stories.the_lesson: Growth in global sport often comes through unlikely pathways — like a heritage-eligible star returning to represent his country of birth at a lower level of competition.

stories.title: IPL stars Klaasen, Miller and Finn Allen sign on for ILT20's star-studded fifth season
key_points: South Africa's **Heinrich Klaasen** and **David Miller** will make their **ILT20 debuts**, both signed by Gulf Giants.
New Zealand's **Finn Allen** also debuts in the league, joining **Abu Dhabi Knight Riders**.
Australia's **Marcus Stoinis** returns to ILT20 after **three years away**, signing with Dubai Capitals.
The UAE's **DP World ILT20** season 5 runs **November 22 to December 20, 2026**.
Franchises like **MI Emirates** have also locked in key retentions, including **Rashid Khan** and **Nicholas Pooran**.
stories.background: The **ILT20** is the UAE's franchise T20 league, launched in 2023 as a winter alternative for global T20 stars during cricket's packed calendar, competing with leagues like South Africa's SA20 and the Caribbean's CPL for the same pool of players. Teams build squads through a mix of retentions from prior seasons and fresh auctions or signings, similar to the IPL model. All these players are established IPL performers, so their arrival raises the league's profile and viewership potential.
stories.what_happened: The DP World ILT20 confirmed a wave of high-profile signings ahead of its fifth season, running **November 22 to December 20, 2026**. South Africa's Heinrich Klaasen and David Miller — both established IPL performers — will make their ILT20 debuts, having signed with Gulf Giants. New Zealand's Finn Allen also debuts in the tournament, joining Abu Dhabi Knight Riders. Australian allrounder Marcus Stoinis returns to the league after a three-year absence to play for Dubai Capitals, which also retained Rovman Powell and Mustafizur Rahman. MI Emirates locked in key players including Nicholas Pooran, Rashid Khan and Romario Shepherd, and added Sherfane Rutherford.
stories.why_it_matters: Landing multiple current IPL stars for their league debuts is a signal of the ILT20's growing pull in the crowded global T20 league market, competing for the same limited pool of star players and broadcast attention as bigger, richer leagues.
stories.ripple_effects: A stronger overseas contingent should lift ILT20's broadcast value and crowds, and adds another data point in the broader trend of franchise T20 leagues competing globally for the same players year-round — intensifying scheduling pressure on international boards trying to fit bilateral cricket around these windows.
stories.why_now: Squad-building news is emerging now because teams are locking in retentions and fresh signings months ahead of the November-December season, giving fans and broadcasters an early look at the rosters.
stories.watch_next: Watch for the full ILT20 season-5 player auction and draft details, and the final squad lists before the November 22 start.

key_terms.definition: The UAE's professional Twenty20 franchise cricket league, played each winter with international and UAE-based players.

stories.the_lesson: As franchise T20 cricket multiplies worldwide, top players are increasingly building year-round, multi-league careers rather than being tied to just their national boards and one home league.

stories.title: Nottinghamshire's cricket boss quits for Lancashire less than a year into the job
key_points: Nottinghamshire CEO **Richard Kenyon** is leaving to become Lancashire's new chief executive.
He only joined Notts in **December 2025**, meaning he departs after **barely eight months**.
He replaces outgoing Lancashire CEO **Daniel Gidney**.
Notts chairman **Andy Hunt** said he's 'disappointed' but understands the pull of Kenyon's home region.
Notts' commercial director **Michael Temple** steps in as **interim CEO** at Trent Bridge.
stories.background: Richard Kenyon built his executive career at Everton Football Club, including a lead role delivering its new Bramley-Moore Dock stadium, before moving into cricket administration. English county cricket clubs like Nottinghamshire (based at Trent Bridge) and Lancashire (based at Old Trafford) are run as separate businesses with their own commercial operations, competing for revenue, sponsorships and top staff much like any sports franchise.
stories.what_happened: Nottinghamshire County Cricket Club confirmed that chief executive Richard Kenyon is leaving to take up the same role at Lancashire, succeeding Lancashire's departing CEO Daniel Gidney. Kenyon had only joined Nottinghamshire in **December 2025**, making his stint at Trent Bridge just over eight months. He previously spent more than a decade at Everton Football Club in senior commercial and community roles. Nottinghamshire's chairman Andy Hunt said he was disappointed Kenyon was leaving so early in his tenure but understood the appeal of a role closer to Kenyon's home region in the northwest of England. The club has appointed commercial director Michael Temple as interim chief executive while it searches for a permanent replacement.
stories.why_it_matters: A quick exit like this highlights how competitive the market for experienced sports executives has become, with counties now poaching each other's leadership the way clubs poach players — and it leaves Nottinghamshire needing fresh leadership stability at short notice.
stories.ripple_effects: Nottinghamshire will need to run its business and commercial operations under interim leadership while it searches for a new permanent CEO, which could slow strategic decisions at the club. Lancashire, meanwhile, gains an executive with a strong stadium-development track record, which could matter for any future ground redevelopment plans at Old Trafford.
stories.why_now: Kenyon's move was announced this week as Lancashire finalized its succession plan following Daniel Gidney's departure.
stories.watch_next: Watch for Nottinghamshire's timeline and shortlist for a permanent chief executive replacement.
stories.the_lesson: Sports organizations compete for management talent just as fiercely as they compete for players — a strong executive track record can trigger a bidding war even outside the transfer window.

stories.title: UAE thrash Canada by 97 runs in World Cup League 2, Rahul Chopra hits unbeaten 127
key_points: **UAE beat Canada by 97 runs** in the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup League 2 in Dundee, Scotland.
UAE posted **282/6** in 50 overs; Canada were bowled out for **185** in 33.4 overs.
**Rahul Chopra** was Player of the Match for an **unbeaten 127**, anchoring UAE's total.
League 2 is a key **qualification pathway** toward the 2027 ODI World Cup for associate nations.
stories.background: **ICC Men's Cricket World Cup League 2** is a multi-year one-day international series that gives cricket's **associate nations** (countries outside the sport's traditional 12 full members, like UAE, Canada, Scotland, Nepal and Oman) a structured route to try to qualify for the next 50-over World Cup, since they don't get automatic entry the way top-ranked teams do. Results across dozens of matches over several years determine which teams advance toward the qualifying tournament.
stories.what_happened: In the **125th match** of League 2, played at **Forthill, Dundee**, the **United Arab Emirates beat Canada by 97 runs**. Batting first, UAE posted **282 for 6** in their 50 overs, built around an **unbeaten 127 from Rahul Chopra**, who was named Player of the Match. Canada's chase never got close, folding for **185** in 33.4 overs. The win strengthens UAE's position in the League 2 standings as the qualification race for the **2027 ODI World Cup** continues.
stories.why_it_matters: For associate cricket nations like the UAE, results in League 2 directly determine whether they get a shot at playing in the next men's 50-over World Cup — a tournament that brings far greater funding, exposure and player development opportunities than they normally receive.
stories.ripple_effects: A strong League 2 campaign helps UAE Cricket's push for greater ICC funding and player contracts, while a poor one for Canada adds pressure on their board, which has already missed direct qualification in past cycles.
stories.why_now: This was one of the scheduled League 2 fixtures in the current qualifying window, played today in Dundee.
stories.watch_next: Watch the League 2 points table over the rest of this window to see which associate nations stay in contention for 2027 World Cup qualification.

key_terms.definition: A cricket-playing country (like UAE, Canada, or Nepal) that is an ICC member but not one of the sport's 12 'full member' nations — associates usually have to qualify through events like League 2 rather than getting automatic entry to major tournaments.

stories.the_lesson: For teams outside a sport's elite tier, qualification tournaments matter as much as the main event — years of unglamorous league matches, not one big final, decide who even gets a seat at the table.

stories.title: ICC confirms 12 venues across South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia for the 2027 Cricket World Cup
key_points: The **2027 Men's Cricket World Cup** will be co-hosted by **South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia**.
**14 teams** will play **57 matches** across the tournament.
**South Africa hosts 8 venues**, including Wanderers (Johannesburg), Newlands (Cape Town) and Centurion.
**Zimbabwe gets 3 venues**, including the newly built **Mosi-oa-Tunya Stadium** in Victoria Falls.
It's the tournament's **first return to Africa since 2003**, when South Africa last hosted.
stories.background: The Cricket World Cup rotates among cricket's major nations, and Africa has hosted only once before — **South Africa in 2003**. Zimbabwe and Namibia have never hosted a men's World Cup match at this scale; folding them into a joint hosting arrangement with South Africa is partly about **spreading the sport's growth and infrastructure investment** across the region, similar to how football's World Cup has occasionally used multi-country hosting.
stories.what_happened: The **International Cricket Council (ICC)** formally confirmed the **12 venues** for the 2027 Men's Cricket World Cup, unveiling the host cities and tournament brand in a launch ceremony. **South Africa** will host the bulk of the tournament across **8 grounds** — Wanderers Stadium (Johannesburg), SuperSport Park (Centurion), Newlands (Cape Town), Kingsmead (Durban), St George's Park (Gqeberha), Mangaung Oval (Bloemfontein), Boland Park (Paarl) and Buffalo Park (East London). **Zimbabwe** contributes **3 venues** — Harare Sports Club, Queens Sports Club in Bulawayo, and the newly constructed **Mosi-oa-Tunya International Cricket Stadium** in Victoria Falls, built specifically for this tournament. **Namibia** hosts matches at its **National Cricket Ground in Windhoek**. In total, **14 teams** will contest **57 matches**, and the event marks the tournament's first trip to Africa since South Africa hosted alone in 2003.
stories.why_it_matters: A brand-new stadium built specifically for the tournament (Victoria Falls) and expanded hosting duties for Zimbabwe and Namibia signal the ICC's push to **grow cricket's footprint and infrastructure in Africa**, beyond the traditional strongholds of South Asia, England and Australia.
stories.ripple_effects: Expect a **tourism and infrastructure boost** for the host nations in the lead-up to 2027, along with increased broadcast and sponsorship interest in African cricket markets. It also raises the profile of **Zimbabwe and Namibia's own national teams**, who will play as co-hosts with automatic qualification interest.
stories.why_now: The ICC unveiled the venues and tournament brand this week as part of its standard multi-year planning cycle ahead of the 2027 event.
stories.watch_next: Watch for the qualification pathway and fixture schedule to be announced next, which will confirm which teams play at which venues.
stories.the_lesson: Major sporting events are increasingly used as tools to build permanent infrastructure and grow a sport in new regions, not just to crown a champion.

stories.title: SunRisers Leeds Women stun Manchester Super Giants to set up Hundred eliminator against Southern Brave
key_points: **SunRisers Leeds Women** beat **Manchester Super Giants** by **41 runs** in a winner-takes-all group match.
**Annabel Sutherland's unbeaten 62 off 36 balls** powered Leeds' innings.
The reigning champions now face **Southern Brave** in an **eliminator on August 14** for a place in the final.
**Trent Rockets** already topped the women's table and go straight into the final without playing the eliminator.
stories.background: The Hundred is English cricket's short-form franchise competition, played in 100-ball innings, with separate men's and women's tournaments run in parallel across the same eight city-based teams. SunRisers Leeds are the reigning women's champions. With the group stage wrapping up, final places and playoff spots were still being decided by results on the last matchday, making today's Leeds-Manchester match a straight knockout for a shot at the eliminator.
stories.what_happened: In a winner-takes-all final group match at Old Trafford, **SunRisers Leeds Women beat Manchester Super Giants Women by 41 runs**, with **Annabel Sutherland's unbeaten 62 off just 36 balls** anchoring Leeds' total. The win means Leeds **leapfrogged Manchester** in the standings and secured second place behind **Trent Rockets**, who had already topped the table on points and qualified directly for the final. Leeds will now play **Southern Brave**, who finished the group stage third, in an **eliminator on August 14**, with the winner advancing to face Trent Rockets in the final.
stories.why_it_matters: The result turns what looked like a straightforward group-stage finish into an extra knockout fixture, adding a sudden-death eliminator to the competition's business end.
stories.ripple_effects: Sutherland's innings strengthens her case for a starring role in the eliminator and boosts her broader reputation as a franchise all-rounder. Fans and broadcasters get an extra high-stakes fixture before the final.
stories.why_now: Today's match was the last of the group stage, directly deciding who would finish second and who would face an eliminator instead of going straight through.
stories.watch_next: The August 14 eliminator between SunRisers Leeds and Southern Brave, with the winner to face Trent Rockets in the final.

key_terms.definition: An English short-form cricket competition where each team bats a 100-ball innings, shorter than the more common 120-ball Twenty20 format.
A knockout match used to decide who advances to a final when a straightforward group-stage finish doesn't produce a clear qualifier.

stories.the_lesson: In league formats decided by fine margins and permutations, a single close finish can flip who's left playing for the title — nothing is settled until the last ball of the group stage.

stories.title: Ravindra Jadeja returns from career-threatening elbow injury as India name Test squad for Sri Lanka; Bumrah ruled out
key_points: **Ravindra Jadeja** returns to India's Test squad for the first time since a **tennis elbow injury** sidelined him in May.
**Jasprit Bumrah** was originally picked but has now been **ruled out through injury**.
**KL Rahul** is named **vice-captain** under Test skipper **Shubman Gill**.
Uncapped all-rounder **Saransh Jain** earns a **maiden Test call-up** after strong domestic form.
The two-match series opens in **Galle on August 15**, with the second Test in Colombo.
stories.background: Jadeja is one of India's most important players — a left-arm spinner and lower-order batter whose all-round skill lets India field a more balanced, attacking XI, especially on the slow, turning pitches typical of the subcontinent. He injured his elbow in May 2026 and hasn't played for India since a January ODI against New Zealand, missing several months of international cricket during his recovery. Bumrah, India's premier fast bowler, has been managed carefully through injury in recent years given how central he is to India's pace attack. Shubman Gill leads India's Test side, with the squad for this tour finalized just days before the series begins.
stories.what_happened: India's selection committee announced a 15-member Test squad for the tour of Sri Lanka, confirming Ravindra Jadeja's return to the setup for the first time since his **tennis elbow injury in May** ended his involvement in India's home international season. Jadeja had been out of the frame for months as he recovered; his selection now signals selectors are confident in his fitness ahead of two Tests starting August 15 in Galle. In a late change, **Jasprit Bumrah, initially named in the squad, was ruled out because of injury**, a blow to India's pace attack for the series. **KL Rahul was confirmed as vice-captain** to Shubman Gill, and uncapped all-rounder **Saransh Jain**, a standout performer in India's domestic first-class competition, earned a **maiden Test call-up**. The squad announcement follows a build-up in which Gill himself had faced fitness questions over a finger injury sustained in practice, since resolved.
stories.why_it_matters: Jadeja's return restores balance to India's XI on pitches where spin and all-round depth matter most, while Bumrah's absence tests the depth of India's pace bowling stocks heading into a Test series against a Sri Lanka side playing at home.
stories.ripple_effects: Saransh Jain's call-up gives India a fresh spin-bowling option to develop for future series. Bumrah's continued injury management fuels an ongoing debate in Indian cricket about workload and how much fast-bowling can be asked of him across formats. Jadeja's fitness through the series will be closely watched given how recently he returned from injury.
stories.why_now: The squad had to be finalized just days ahead of the first Test on August 15, with selectors needing final clarity on both Jadeja's and Bumrah's fitness before naming the touring party.
stories.watch_next: Jadeja's workload and form in the first Test at Galle starting August 15, and whether Bumrah is available later in the series or rested for the full tour.

key_terms.definition: An overuse injury causing pain around the elbow, common in sports involving repetitive arm motion like bowling.
The deputy to a team's captain, who takes over leadership duties if the captain is unavailable.

stories.the_lesson: In team sport, squad depth — having a ready replacement like a domestic standout waiting for their chance — matters as much as star power, because injuries to key players are inevitable over a long season.

stories.title: West Indies miss direct qualification for the 2027 ODI World Cup for the third straight time
key_points: West Indies' hopes of **direct qualification** for the 2027 ODI World Cup are mathematically over.
**Afghanistan's** series-clinching win over Ireland took the last automatic qualification spot, confirmed in reports through **August 10-11**.
The top **8** ODI-ranked teams as of **September 30, 2026** qualify directly; West Indies sit **10th** and can't climb high enough even with two games left against India.
It's the **third consecutive World Cup** the two-time champions (1975, 1979) must reach via a qualifier, set for **February 2027**.
The 2027 World Cup will be co-hosted by **South Africa, Zimbabwe, and Namibia** — the first time it's held in Africa.
stories.background: West Indies won the first two Cricket World Cups ever played, in 1975 and 1979, and were once cricket's dominant force, but the men's ODI team has declined sharply over the past decade. They also missed direct qualification for the 2023 World Cup and had to win a qualifying tournament just to reach that event. Qualification for 2027 is based on each team's ICC ODI ranking as of a set cutoff date, with the top 8 teams (excluding co-hosts) going through automatically.
stories.what_happened: Afghanistan beat Ireland by 92 runs in a rain-affected second ODI at Bready Cricket Club, Belfast, clinching the eighth and final automatic World Cup qualification spot alongside defending champions Australia, India, New Zealand, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, England, and Bangladesh. West Indies sit 10th in the ICC ODI rankings and still have two ODIs against India before the September 30 cutoff, but even winning both would not be enough to climb into the top 8. Co-hosts South Africa and Zimbabwe (with Namibia as a third venue) qualify automatically as tournament hosts regardless of ranking. West Indies will now have to navigate a qualifier tournament in **February 2027** just to reach the 14-team, 57-match main event.
stories.why_it_matters: It's a stark marker of continued decline for a storied cricket nation, and a real commercial and competitive concern for West Indies cricket, which now faces genuine risk of missing the World Cup altogether — as has happened to other once-dominant teams in recent qualifying cycles.
stories.ripple_effects: It adds pressure on West Indies' upcoming home ODI series against India, even though those results can no longer change their direct-qualification fate, and sharpens focus on selection and personnel decisions ahead of the February 2027 qualifier.
stories.why_now: Afghanistan's win over Ireland eliminated the last mathematical scenario for West Indies to break into the automatic top 8 before the ranking cutoff, with the fallout confirmed in reports through August 10-11.
stories.watch_next: Confirmed venues and the participant list for the February 2027 ODI World Cup Qualifier, and West Indies' squad calls for their upcoming series against India.

key_terms.definition: One Day International — a format of cricket where each team bats for a fixed 50 overs, distinct from the shorter T20 format or multi-day Test matches.

stories.the_lesson: In ranking-based qualification systems, results from other teams' matches can end your own tournament hopes before you've played your remaining games — a reminder that in sport, as in many competitive systems, your fate isn't always in your own hands.

stories.title: IPL wicketkeeper Abhishek Porel arrested in rape and blackmail case
key_points: **Delhi Capitals and Bengal** wicketkeeper-batter **Abhishek Porel**, 23, was arrested by West Bengal police on **August 11, 2026**.
The arrest followed a **Calcutta High Court order** directing police to act 'immediately' and seize his electronic devices.
A medical student alleges a **3.5-year relationship**, a physical relationship on the promise of marriage, and that Porel later threatened to circulate intimate images.
He's charged under multiple sections of the **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita** plus **IT Act** provisions covering privacy violation and blackmail.
Delhi Capitals **retained Porel for ₹4 crore** (about $480,000) for IPL 2026; the franchise had not commented as of the arrest.
stories.background: Porel is a young wicketkeeper-batter who plays for Delhi Capitals in the **Indian Premier League (IPL)** — India's richest domestic T20 competition — and for Bengal in domestic cricket. The complaint was originally lodged in June by a third-year medical student from Karnataka, who says the pair met in January 2023 and were in a relationship for roughly three-and-a-half years, including trips abroad together, before Porel denied the relationship and allegedly threatened to circulate intimate photos and videos of her.
stories.what_happened: Mogra police in West Bengal's Hooghly district arrested Porel on Tuesday, August 11, and produced him before a court in Chinsurah. The arrest followed a July 20 Calcutta High Court order that directed police to arrest him 'immediately' and seize his electronic devices to protect the complainant's privacy — a directive police took roughly three weeks to act on. The complainant alleges Porel took her to his flat in Mankundu and had a physical relationship with her on the promise of marriage, and that he later denied the relationship and threatened to circulate intimate images and videos of her. Police have registered the case under multiple sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita — India's criminal code — covering sexual offences, plus sections of the IT Act covering privacy violation and image-based blackmail. Porel denies the allegations.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a serious criminal case against an active, high-value IPL player rather than a form or fitness story, and raises questions about how Delhi Capitals and Bengal's cricket association will handle a contracted player facing serious charges.
stories.ripple_effects: Delhi Capitals may face pressure to comment on or review Porel's contract status; the case could also affect his availability for Bengal's domestic season, and adds to scrutiny of how IPL franchises respond when contracted players face serious legal allegations.
stories.why_now: The arrest happened today, roughly three weeks after the High Court's directive, following a slower initial police response.
stories.watch_next: The bail hearing outcome in Chinsurah court, and whether Delhi Capitals or the BCCI issue a statement on his contract status.

key_terms.definition: India's criminal code that replaced the colonial-era Indian Penal Code in 2024, covering offences including sexual assault and criminal intimidation.

stories.the_lesson: A sports league's commercial value doesn't shield contracted athletes from ordinary legal accountability — franchises increasingly have to navigate reputational and contractual questions when a player faces serious criminal allegations.

stories.title: Shubman Gill returns to batting pain-free, clearing the last doubt before India's Sri Lanka Tests

thread.previously: We reported Gill took a fresh finger knock during the India A warm-up win over Sri Lanka XI but was provisionally cleared for the first Test.
thread.changed: Gill has now batted in the nets fully pain-free, removing the lingering doubt over his fitness heading into the August 15 Galle Test.

key_points: India captain **Shubman Gill** batted in the nets **pain-free** on Sunday, easing fitness fears before the Sri Lanka Tests.
Gill had been hit on his **right ring finger** during a practice session on **Thursday**, forcing him out of the three-day warm-up match.
**KL Rahul** led India in that warm-up game with Gill sidelined; Gill's return removes the doubt over his availability.
The first Test starts in **Galle on August 15**, with the second at Colombo's **SSC Ground from August 23-27**.
Team management called the injury **"just a precaution more than anything else."**
stories.background: **Shubman Gill** is India's Test captain, and his fitness heading into an away series matters both for India's batting lineup and team leadership continuity. India already went into this **Sri Lanka tour with injury concerns**, having lost key players including **Jasprit Bumrah and Washington Sundar** to injury ahead of the series. Gill was hit on his right ring finger during a practice session last Thursday, serious enough that he sat out the subsequent three-day warm-up match against a Sri Lanka Cricket XI, with vice-captain **KL Rahul** leading the side in his place.
stories.what_happened: Gill returned to batting practice in the nets on **Sunday**, showing no visible discomfort after his right ring-finger injury. He had missed India's three-day warm-up match against Sri Lanka Cricket XI as a precaution after being hit on the finger during practice the previous Thursday, with KL Rahul captaining in his absence. Assistant coach Bahutule said the decision to rest him for the warm-up game was "just a precaution more than anything else." With Gill now batting freely, India's camp has one less injury doubt heading into a series they've already approached short-handed, having also lost Bumrah and Washington Sundar to unrelated injuries. The first Test begins in **Galle on August 15**, with the second and final Test at Colombo's SSC Ground from **August 23-27**.
stories.why_it_matters: Losing a captain to injury just before a Test series would have forced India into leadership and batting-order changes on short notice; Gill's clean return removes that risk and lets India go into the series at closer to full strength, even with Bumrah and Washington Sundar still missing.
stories.ripple_effects: A fit Gill stabilizes India's batting order and captaincy continuity for the series opener. It also reduces the pressure on KL Rahul, who would otherwise have had to juggle vice-captaincy duties with stepping into the top job on short notice.
stories.why_now: Gill's return to full training happened now because it's the last practical checkpoint before the squad finalizes its XI for the first Test, which starts August 15.
stories.watch_next: Watch India's playing XI announcement ahead of the August 15 Galle Test for final confirmation of Gill's fitness and batting position.
stories.the_lesson: In team sports, a leader's physical availability is itself a strategic asset — teams build contingency plans around captaincy and key personnel precisely because a single injury can cascade into batting order, leadership, and morale changes all at once.

stories.title: Afghanistan beat Ireland to clinch the ODI series and book a direct spot at the 2027 World Cup

thread.previously: We previewed Afghanistan's 3rd ODI against Ireland in Belfast as a series-clinching match with 2027 World Cup qualification points on the line.
thread.changed: Afghanistan won that match by 3 wickets, clinching the series 2-0 and securing direct qualification for the 2027 ODI World Cup.

key_points: Afghanistan beat Ireland by **3 wickets** in the 3rd ODI in Belfast, sealing the series **2-0**.
The win secures Afghanistan's **direct qualification for the 2027 ODI World Cup**, sparing them a qualifying tournament.
Leg-spinner **Rashid Khan** was central to the campaign, having taken a **six-wicket haul** in the 2nd ODI.
Afghanistan chased down Ireland's total with **31 balls to spare** in the decisive match.
The result caps a dominant series for Afghanistan, one of the format's fastest-rising teams.
stories.background: Afghanistan have become one of the most competitive white-ball teams in world cricket over the past decade, built around a core of skilled spin bowlers led by **Rashid Khan**, one of the format's best leg-spinners. Direct qualification for the 50-over **ODI World Cup** is determined by teams' rankings and performance in the current cycle — missing it means playing in a separate, high-pressure qualifying tournament against other associate and lower-ranked nations, so a direct spot removes a major source of risk two years out from the 2027 tournament. Ireland, an associate-turned-full-member nation, hosted Afghanistan for a five-match ODI series this month, giving both sides valuable rankings points and match practice.
stories.what_happened: Afghanistan beat Ireland by **3 wickets** in the 3rd ODI in Belfast on August 10, successfully chasing down Ireland's total with **31 balls to spare**. The win gave Afghanistan an unassailable **2-0 series lead** (after the first match was abandoned to rain) and, with it, direct qualification for the **2027 ODI World Cup** — avoiding a separate qualifying tournament. **Rashid Khan** was a key figure across the series, having taken a **six-wicket haul** in the 2nd ODI alongside a strong batting contribution from Ibrahim Zadran. The series continues with two more dead-rubber matches before it concludes on August 14.
stories.why_it_matters: Direct World Cup qualification is a significant competitive and financial milestone — it guarantees Afghanistan a place at cricket's biggest 50-over event without the risk of an upset in a qualifier, and reinforces their standing as a genuine top-tier ODI side rather than a plucky underdog.
stories.ripple_effects: Ireland, by contrast, now faces a tougher road to secure their own World Cup spot and will need results elsewhere in the qualification cycle. Afghanistan's cricket board gains leverage and prestige from direct qualification, which also affects other teams' World Cup qualification math since spots are relative to the field.
stories.why_now: The result decided the series and the qualification question in the same match, because Afghanistan needed this specific win to both clinch the series and lock in enough qualification points.
stories.watch_next: Watch the remaining two dead-rubber ODIs (through August 14) for further form guides ahead of Afghanistan's build-up to 2027, and Ireland's path through the rest of the qualification cycle.

key_terms.definition: Earning a spot at a tournament automatically through rankings/results, without having to win a separate qualifying event.

stories.the_lesson: In sports built around ranking cycles, a single match can carry weight far beyond its own scoreline — the same result can decide a series and a multi-year qualification path at once.

stories.title: Trent Rockets Men clinch an automatic Hundred final spot, topping the table on 28 points
key_points: Trent Rockets Men beat **Southern Brave** in their final group match to top the table on **28 points**.
The win secures an **automatic spot in Sunday's final** at Lord's, skipping the eliminator entirely.
It caps the men's team's **strongest-ever Hundred campaign**, capping a dominant group stage.
The men's final is on **August 16**; an eliminator on August 14 decides who joins them.
This is a separate storyline from Trent Rockets' **women's** team, who also topped their own group this week.
stories.background: The Hundred is England's short-format 100-ball cricket competition, running men's and women's tournaments in parallel with matching team names and shared venues. Trent Rockets — based at Trent Bridge, Nottingham — have had contrasting histories in the men's and women's competitions since the tournament launched in 2021. Eight teams compete in each group stage, with the top two advancing straight to the final and the next two playing an eliminator for the remaining final spot.
stories.what_happened: Trent Rockets Men beat **Southern Brave** on Monday, August 10, in their final group-stage match, finishing on top of the men's Hundred table with **28 points** from their eight matches. Topping the table gives them **automatic qualification for Sunday's final** at Lord's, meaning they skip Friday's eliminator between the second- and third-placed teams entirely. It caps a dominant group stage in which the Rockets won the bulk of their fixtures, having already sealed a top-three finish and a knockout spot earlier in the tournament after beating MI London. The result is separate from — and coincides with — Trent Rockets' **women's** team also finishing top of their own group this week, giving the club a strong showing across both competitions.
stories.why_it_matters: Finishing top means Trent Rockets avoid the extra elimination-match risk that the second- and third-placed sides face, giving them a rest advantage and a straight run at the title.
stories.ripple_effects: For the four teams below them — Southern Brave included — Monday's result reshuffled who plays the eliminator and who's already out, with real financial and reputational stakes for players hoping to catch the eye of national selectors.
stories.why_now: Monday's match was the last of the men's group stage, making it the deciding fixture for who finishes top of the table.
stories.watch_next: Watch Friday's eliminator (August 14) to see who joins Trent Rockets in Sunday's final at Lord's.

key_terms.definition: An English short-format cricket competition where each innings is 100 balls, bowled in five-ball 'sets' instead of six-ball overs, run separately for men's and women's teams.

stories.the_lesson: In knockout-adjacent formats, finishing first isn't just about bragging rights — it buys a bye past an elimination round that lower-ranked teams have to survive.

stories.title: India A beat Sri Lanka XI in their warm-up match as captain Shubman Gill takes a fresh finger knock but is cleared for the first Test
key_points: India completed a **six-wicket win** over Sri Lanka Cricket XI, chasing 207 with Jaiswal and Gill sharing a **105-run opening stand**.
Captain **Shubman Gill** took a fresh impact injury to his right ring finger during the match and sat out Day 1 fielding as a precaution.
Gill was cleared by the medical team and **batted on Day 3**, easing fitness doubts before the first Test.
**Devdutt Padikkal** anchored India's first innings with an unbeaten 142; Mohammed Siraj smashed 32 off 15 balls late in the chase.
The result sets India up for the **first Test against Sri Lanka in Galle, starting August 15**.
stories.background: Shubman Gill was named India's new Test captain ahead of this tour and had already been nursing concerns over a finger injury heading into the warm-up match, alongside the separate loss of strike bowler Jasprit Bumrah, who was ruled out of the entire series. The three-day warm-up fixture against a Sri Lanka Cricket XI, played at the Nondescripts Cricket Club ground in Colombo starting August 7, was designed to get India's batters and bowlers accustomed to subcontinental conditions before the first Test at Galle.
stories.what_happened: India A chased down a target of 207 to beat Sri Lanka Cricket XI by **six wickets** in their three-day warm-up match in Colombo, with Yashasvi Jaiswal and captain Shubman Gill putting on a **105-run opening stand**. During the match, Gill sustained a fresh impact injury to his right ring finger and did not take the field on Day 1 as a precaution, adding to existing concerns about his fitness. However, India's medical team cleared him to bat on Day 3, and he did so without visible discomfort, easing fears he might miss the start of the series. Devdutt Padikkal had earlier anchored India's first innings with an unbeaten 142, while Mohammed Siraj provided a late flourish in the chase, smashing 32 off just 15 balls including three successive sixes. Jaiswal, who had been dismissed for a duck in the first innings, responded with a quickfire 61 off 46 balls in the second.
stories.why_it_matters: Gill's fitness is critical for India both as captain and opening/top-order batter heading into a five-Test tour already missing lead pacer Jasprit Bumrah — losing him too would have been a major blow to India's plans in Sri Lanka.
stories.ripple_effects: A confident warm-up win, plus Gill's fitness clearance, gives India momentum heading into the series opener; how the bowling attack — already missing Bumrah — performs in these conditions will shape team selection for the first Test.
stories.why_now: The warm-up match was the last on-field test of form and fitness before India's squad finalizes its XI for the first Test, which starts August 15 in Galle.
stories.watch_next: Watch India's team selection announcement ahead of the first Test at Galle on August 15, particularly whether Gill is fully passed fit to bat and lead without restriction.
stories.the_lesson: In cricket, warm-up matches exist precisely to surface fitness and form issues before they matter in a real Test — a niggle that shows up in a practice game is far cheaper to manage than one that appears mid-series.

thread.previously: We reported Gill batting pain-free in the nets, which had eased fitness fears ahead of the first Test after he had been nursing a finger injury.

stories.title: Nepal names Sandeep Lamichhane its new ODI captain, replacing Rohit Paudel ahead of the ACC Premier Cup
key_points: Leg-spinner **Sandeep Lamichhane**, who has taken 154 wickets in 77 ODIs, becomes Nepal's ODI captain again.
He replaces **Rohit Paudel**, under whom Nepal won 11 of 12 ODIs in the ICC Cricket World Cup League 2.
It's Lamichhane's **second stint** as captain — his first ended in 2022 when he was suspended after an arrest warrant.
The change comes ahead of the **ACC Men's Premier Cup**, running in Malaysia from **August 30 to September 12**.
At 26, Lamichhane is one of Nepal's most recognizable cricketers and a T20 franchise regular worldwide.
stories.background: Nepal has become one of the more competitive Associate cricket nations over the past several years, regularly punching above its weight in qualifying tournaments. Sandeep Lamichhane, a leg-spin bowler who has played in T20 leagues around the world, previously captained Nepal before being suspended by the Cricket Association of Nepal (CAN) in 2022 after an arrest warrant was issued against him; Rohit Paudel then took over and led the side successfully, including an 11-from-12 ODI winning run in the ICC Cricket World Cup League 2, a tournament that feeds into qualification for the 50-over World Cup.
stories.what_happened: The Cricket Association of Nepal named **Sandeep Lamichhane** as the team's new ODI captain, taking over from Rohit Paudel, who had led the side successfully including winning 11 of 12 matches in the ICC Cricket World Cup League 2. It marks Lamichhane's second stint in charge, after his first was cut short in 2022 when CAN suspended him following an arrest warrant. His first assignment as captain will be the **ACC Men's Premier Cup**, an Asian regional tournament being held in Malaysia from August 30 to September 12.
stories.why_it_matters: Nepal is trying to build toward a stronger long-term standing in world cricket, and a captaincy change right before a major regional tournament is a significant call on leadership at a pivotal moment for the team's qualification ambitions.
stories.ripple_effects: How Lamichhane performs as captain will shape Nepal's showing at the ACC Premier Cup and feed into broader narratives about Associate-nation cricket's development; it could also affect Paudel's role and standing within the squad going forward.
stories.why_now: The change was made specifically ahead of the ACC Premier Cup later this month, giving the new leadership group time to settle before a tournament with regional qualification stakes.
stories.watch_next: Watch Nepal's opening matches at the ACC Premier Cup starting August 30 for early signs of how the team responds to the leadership change.
stories.the_lesson: In team sports, leadership changes right before a major tournament are a calculated bet — teams often prioritize a captain's experience or public profile over continuity, even when the outgoing leader was winning.

stories.title: PNG Women win last-ball thriller over Thailand to take 1-0 T20I series lead
key_points: Papua New Guinea Women beat Thailand Women by **5 wickets**, winning off the **very last ball** of the innings.
PNG chased down Thailand's **109/5** to finish **110/5 in 20 overs**.
Thailand's top scorers were **Phannita Maya (35)** and **Nannapat Koncharoenkai (30)**.
PNG's **Isabel Toua** was Player of the Match, taking **3 wickets for 13 runs**.
The result puts PNG **1-0 up** in the two-match T20I series.
stories.background: Papua New Guinea and Thailand are both associate cricket nations — countries where cricket is growing but not yet at the top international tier of teams like India, Australia, or England. Women's cricket in these associate nations has been expanding steadily, with more bilateral series and World Cup qualifying pathways giving teams like PNG and Thailand regular competitive cricket. This two-match T20I series in Port Moresby, PNG's capital, is part of that growing associate-nation cricket calendar.
stories.what_happened: Papua New Guinea Women beat Thailand Women by **5 wickets** in the first T20I of their two-match series at Port Moresby on August 10, chasing down Thailand's total of **109/5** with the winning run coming off the **very last ball** of the innings, finishing on 110/5 in 20 overs. Thailand's innings was built around contributions from **Phannita Maya (35)** and **Nannapat Koncharoenkai (30)**. For PNG, bowler **Isabel Toua** was named Player of the Match after taking **3 wickets for just 13 runs**, helping restrict Thailand's total and setting up the tight chase. The win puts PNG **1-0 up** in the two-match series.
stories.why_it_matters: For associate cricket nations like PNG and Thailand, every close, competitive match like this builds the case for more funding, fixtures, and visibility for women's cricket outside the sport's traditional powerhouses. A last-ball finish is also a reminder that associate cricket produces genuine drama, not just development games.
stories.ripple_effects: A series win for PNG would boost their standing and momentum heading into future qualifying tournaments for global events. Strong performances by both teams help build the case for more regular fixtures against higher-ranked nations, which is how associate teams typically improve fastest.
stories.why_now: The match was the first of a fresh two-match bilateral series that just got underway in Port Moresby, with the series decider still to come.
stories.watch_next: Watch the second and final T20I of the series for whether PNG completes a series sweep or Thailand levels it.

key_terms.definition: Twenty20 International — the shortest official cricket format between national teams, with each side batting for a maximum of 20 overs.
A cricket-playing country, like PNG or Thailand, that is a full member of the ICC but not yet in the sport's top competitive tier.

stories.the_lesson: Close, last-ball finishes aren't unique to the sport's biggest teams — they're a sign that a contest, at any level, has real, high-quality competition on both sides.

stories.title: Trent Rockets Women fight back from 10-3 to beat Southern Brave and seal a spot in the Hundred final

thread.previously: We reported that Trent Rockets Women could seal top spot in the group stage with a win over Southern Brave, setting up a direct route to Sunday's final at Lord's.
thread.changed: They've now done it: Trent Rockets Women won by 3 wickets with 2 balls to spare, capping a comeback from 10-3 — the lowest powerplay score in the competition's history — to book their place in the final.

key_points: Trent Rockets Women won by **3 wickets with 2 balls remaining**, sealing top spot
Collapsed to **10 for 3** in the powerplay — the **lowest powerplay score** in Hundred history
**Nat Sciver-Brunt** hit an unbeaten 32 off 19 balls to steady the chase
Their **seventh straight win** of the competition
Goes straight to the **final at Lord's on August 16**, skipping the eliminator
stories.background: The Hundred is England's 100-ball franchise cricket competition, with eight teams in men's and women's editions. The team that finishes **top of the table** after eight group games goes straight to the final, while second and third play an eliminator for the other spot — meaning table position matters as much as winning any single match. Trent Rockets Women had been building toward this all tournament, arriving at this match on a six-match winning streak.
stories.what_happened: **Trent Rockets Women** beat **Southern Brave Women by 3 wickets with 2 balls remaining** at Trent Bridge, Nottingham, sealing top spot in the group table and a direct place in **The Hundred final at Lord's on Sunday, August 16**. Chasing Southern Brave's 117 for 5, Trent Rockets collapsed to **10 for 3 in the powerplay — the lowest powerplay score in the competition's history** — before **Nat Sciver-Brunt** anchored the recovery, batting down the order and smashing **32 off just 19 balls** to help the Rockets reach 118 for 7. The win was Trent Rockets' **seventh straight victory** in the competition. As group-stage winners, they bypass Friday's eliminator at The Kia Oval, where the second and third-placed teams play for the other final spot.
stories.why_it_matters: Finishing top means Trent Rockets Women get a rest before the final while their rivals play a win-or-go-home eliminator — a real competitive advantage heading into the tournament's biggest match.
stories.ripple_effects: Southern Brave and the two teams below them now fight it out for the second final spot at the Kia Oval eliminator on August 14; Nat Sciver-Brunt's form as a finisher adds to her case as one of the tournament's standout players heading into the final.
stories.why_now: This was the final group-stage match that could mathematically confirm Trent Rockets Women's top spot, which is why it carried direct qualification stakes.
stories.watch_next: The Kia Oval eliminator on August 14 to see who joins Trent Rockets Women in Sunday's final at Lord's.

stories.the_lesson: In tournaments with a table-topper's bye, the regular season isn't just about making the playoffs — where you finish changes your path, so contesting every group match for position matters as much as just qualifying.
